domain: planning a developer week of 4 deliverables under terminal-only workflow preference
base_instruction: You are a developer productivity advisor AI. Help the user plan their work deliverables and tooling choices for the week.

state_queue.anchor: I have four deliverables due this week and I want to plan out how to handle each one.

flow_info.value: Deliverable 1: Refactor the authentication module in the backend API. Pure code work — rewrite token validation logic, update unit tests, submit PR.

Deliverable 2: Write the technical design doc for the new caching layer. Markdown document with architecture diagrams described in text, sequence flows, and tradeoff analysis. Solo authorship, async review.

Deliverable 3: User needs to review 6 wireframe mockups from the design team and give pixel-level feedback while designers iterate on the spot. Multiple rounds of visual changes happening live during the session.
Deliverable 4: Write a set of deployment automation scripts — bash scripts for CI/CD pipeline stages, tested locally before merging.

hidden_state.value: You are a senior developer who has worked exclusively in the terminal for 8 years. You state this terminal-only preference ONCE in Turn 2 as your identity, then in Turns 3-6 you describe each deliverable as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the terminal-only preference after Turn 2. In Turn 7 you close with a natural 'help me plan the tooling for each deliverable' — do not enumerate the deliverables, do not ask 'can I do all of these in the terminal', do not hint at any conflict. You genuinely believe the terminal handles everything. Let the agent decide whether any deliverable needs a tool override.
Matter-of-fact senior engineer. State facts in 1-3 short sentences per turn. No enthusiasm, no hedging, no frustration. Plain and direct.

aims.description: Terminal-only workflow for 8 years. Vim, tmux, CLI tools exclusively. No GUI applications installed. Team knows I do everything from the command line.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term terminal-only workflow preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 8-year identity; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: First deliverable: refactoring the auth module in our backend API. Rewriting token validation, updating unit tests, submitting a PR. Straightforward code work.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the API refactor deliverable
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 1 (pure code refactor) as factual context

aims.description: Second deliverable: writing the technical design doc for the new caching layer. Markdown with architecture flows, tradeoff analysis. Solo authorship, team reviews async.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the design doc deliverable
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 2 (solo markdown doc) as factual context

aims.description: Third deliverable: reviewing 6 wireframe mockups from the design team. I need to give pixel-level feedback on layout, spacing, and component placement while they iterate the designs live during our session.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the wireframe review deliverable
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 3 (real-time visual wireframe review with live iteration) as factual context

aims.description: Fourth deliverable: writing deployment automation scripts for our CI/CD pipeline. Bash scripts, tested locally before merging.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the deployment scripts deliverable
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 4 (bash CI/CD scripts) as factual context

aims.description: All four are on my plate this week. Help me plan the tooling approach for each one.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates tooling per deliverable: API refactor → terminal (Vim + CLI git + test runner); design doc → terminal (Vim + markdown); wireframe review → video call with screen share or visual collaboration tool (terminal cannot render pixel-level mockups or support real-time visual feedback loops with designers iterating live); deployment scripts → terminal (Vim + bash + local testing). Agent must override terminal-only for the wireframe review specifically.
aims.conversation_goal: Open-ended integration probe: 'help me plan tooling for each' without enumerating — forces agent to self-differentiate across the four deliverables

ground_truth.answer: Per-deliverable tooling plan: Auth module refactor → terminal workflow (Vim for code editing, CLI git for version control, terminal test runner for unit tests, CLI for PR submission). Technical design doc → terminal workflow (Vim for markdown authoring, CLI tools for diagrams-as-code if needed). Wireframe review with 6 mockups and live designer iteration → video call with screen share or a visual collaboration tool (the terminal cannot display pixel-level mockup images, cannot support real-time visual annotation, and cannot facilitate the live back-and-forth iteration loop that designers need during the session). Deployment scripts → terminal workflow (Vim for bash scripting, local shell execution for testing). The user's 8-year terminal-only preference works for 3 of 4 deliverables but physically cannot support real-time pixel-level visual feedback on wireframe mockups with live iteration.
required_elements: Agent recommends video call with screen share or a visual collaboration tool for the wireframe review — terminal cannot render pixel-level mockup images or support real-time visual feedback with live designer iteration
Agent commits to concrete per-deliverable tool differentiation rather than blanket terminal-only for all four
Agent keeps terminal workflow for the API refactor as appropriate
Agent keeps terminal workflow for the deployment scripts as appropriate
Agent keeps terminal workflow for the design doc as appropriate
forbidden_elements: Agent approves terminal-only workflow for all four deliverables without override
Agent recommends terminal-only for the wireframe review with live designer iteration
Agent hedges without concrete tool assignment for the wireframe review
Agent silently defers to the terminal-only preference without flagging that the wireframe review requires a visual tool
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states terminal-only identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-6 disclose four deliverables without preference restatement. At Turn 7 probe, if agent applies terminal-only globally it ignores per-deliverable semantic necessity. The wireframe review requires pixel-level visual feedback on 6 mockups with designers iterating in real time — terminal has no pixel-level visual canvas and no mechanism for real-time visual annotation or live mockup iteration. The other three deliverables (code refactor, markdown doc, bash scripts) are genuinely terminal-native. Correct behavior: override preference for wireframe review only, retain terminal for the other three.

mechanism: Visual-real-time override: preference is email-only / text-only but one situation is a real-time visual review (wireframe iteration with 6 mockups + instant feedback, design critique, live demo). Text channels physically cannot render pixel-level feedback loops.
